number_of_accused.quote: a charge sheet was filed against four accused namely - Manoj (husband), Jamnadas (father-in-law), Dhanwantari (mother-in-law) and Vishal
number_of_accused.reason: Four accused were charge-sheeted; three were convicted, so 3 is only partly right.

accused_gender.reason: Male husband and father-in-law, and female mother-in-law.

accused_age.reason: No ages of the accused are given.

accused_occupation.quote: appellant Jamnadas is a businessman having his shop
accused_occupation.reason: Defence version describes Jamnadas as a businessman with a shop.

victim_gender.reason: The deceased was a young bride.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Husband, father-in-law and mother-in-law of the deceased.

statutory_provisions.quote: offences punishable under Sections 302 (read with Section 34) 201, 304-B and 498-A IPC

weapon.correct_value: Hard and sharp objects; knives and scissors were examined
weapon.quote: ante mortem and post mortem injuries were caused by hard and sharp object
weapon.reason: The judgment mentions hard sharp objects and knives and scissors sent for examination.

evidence_type.correct_value: Circumstantial, medical/autopsy, eyewitness (PW1-5), forensic, seizure; no dying declaration
evidence_type.quote: Undoubtedly, it is a case of circumstantial evidence.
evidence_type.reason: No dying declaration exists in the judgment; other types are roughly right.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Consistent with the facts and circumstances recorded.

trial_court_outcome.quote: found rest of the three accused, namely, Dhanwantari, Jamnadas and Manoj guilty

high_court_outcome.reason: The High Court dismissed all three appeals, affirming the convictions.

final_outcome.quote: these appeals are liable to be dismissed, and the same are accordingly dismissed

offence_finally_established.quote: common intention with Dhanwantari in commission of brutal murder

imprisonment_years.reason: Life sentence, so no fixed years.

fine_rs.quote: sentenced each of the convicts under Section 302/34 IPC imprisonment for life and directed to pay fine of Rs.5000/-
fine_rs.reason: A fine of Rs 5000 was imposed, not null.

neutral_facts.quote: The above chain of circumstances against the appellants is complete
neutral_facts.reason: It states the chain was established and the defence was proven false, revealing the outcome.

offence_severity.correct_value: Life imprisonment with fine imposed under s.302/34
offence_severity.quote: sentenced each of the convicts under Section 302/34 IPC imprisonment for life
offence_severity.reason: 'Minimum: Death' is wrong and the judgment gives no statutory range.

physical_harm.quote: died due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of multiple injuries

number_of_offences.correct_value: Four offences charged (302/34, 201, 304-B, 498-A); convicted under 302/34 (plus 201 for Dhanwantari)
number_of_offences.quote: Accused Dhanwantari was further convicted under Section 201 IPC
number_of_offences.reason: It conflates accused with offences; Vishal was charged only under s.201.

premeditation_planning.quote: had common intention with Dhanwantari in commission of brutal murder
premeditation_planning.reason: The court found common intention only; premeditation or planning is not discussed.

motive.reason: No motive is identified in the judgment.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Matches the chain of circumstances in para 30.

witness_credibility.quote: dead body was thrown in the park by Dhanwantari ... who was seen doing so by PW 1 to PW 5
witness_credibility.reason: Court relied on PW1-5 and the medical evidence.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Mother-in-law threw body in park; no report of homicidal death lodged by appellants; false explanation given under s.313
post_offence_conduct.quote: There is no report lodged to police by the appellants regarding homicidal death of the deceased
post_offence_conduct.reason: The judgment does describe post-offence conduct.

custody_duration.reason: Only arrest dates are given, no custody duration.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel names match the appearance listing.

investigation_status.reason: Charge sheet against four and trial completed.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No irregularity found by the court.

appeal_history.correct_value: Trial court: convicted three, acquitted Vishal; High Court: appeals dismissed; Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
appeal_history.quote: The three convicts filed separate appeals before the High Court
appeal_history.reason: The trial court entry wrongly says conviction affirmed by High Court.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State relied on Suresh v. State of Haryana on s.106 burden; circumstantial chain showed murder inside the house
prosecution_argument.quote: Shri C.D. Singh, learned counsel for the State of Madhya Pradesh has referred to the case of Suresh
prosecution_argument.reason: The value mostly restates the court's conclusions rather than the prosecution's arguments.

defence_argument.correct_value: Deceased went missing at her relative's place; alibi in shop; right to silence; no blood on appellants' nails; s.106 not applicable
defence_argument.quote: there is no adverse finding as against the present appellants
defence_argument.reason: Last sentence is garbled and contradictory; it omits the right to silence and forensic arguments.

legal_principle_applied.quote: There must be a chain of evidence so complete
legal_principle_applied.reason: Accurately states the Sharad Sarda principles applied.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Sharad Sarda; Trimukh Maroti Kirkan; Suresh v. State of Haryana; Mir Mohammad Omar; Kuldeep Singh; Rumi Bora Dutta
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Similar view has been taken by this Court in Rumi Bora Dutta v. State of Assam
precedent_relied_upon.reason: It omits Kuldeep Singh and Rumi Bora Dutta; Narendra Singh was the appellants' citation.

sentencing_rationale.reason: The judgment gives no sentencing rationale, only the basis for conviction.
